svg.text: D237: where the keyhole standoff goes, a panel's top-left corner tile, from the front, to scale

g.text: a and b, where panels meet (open corner)
Green: a, 12 x 21 mm pad, keyhole cut in it, the screw (black) at
rest. Blue dashes: b, 13 x 22. Grey dots: today's standoff.
Red circle: a's nearest point to a slot or a hook's tab.
a at a wall's outer corner (closed)
The same spot on every panel, so the wall's screws
make one regular pattern.
c at a closed corner: 2 mm clear
c keeps 2 mm at closed corners, but its spot differs
from an open corner's, so a wall needs two screw patterns.
2 mm clear round each slot and its chamfer (C83)
a hook's back tab: 4.5 mm wide, 8.25 mm below the slot
panel edge (a seam when open)
Through the keyhole, from the side (option a, 4 mm screw)
wall
lips 1.5
head's channel 3.5
roof and standoff, to 15 mm
board 5
down
The screw stands about 5 mm out of the wall. The board goes on with
its head through the entry (the wide hole, below), then drops: the
shank slides up the 4.5 mm slot in the 1.5 mm lips, and the head is
held behind them in its channel, as the slot clip's keyhole does
(C199). The board's face is left plain; the standoff is 15 mm (D238).
a: walls 1.5 mm round the keyhole: 1.28 mm clear of every slot and
hook where panels meet, 1.50 mm at a wall's outer corner.
b: walls 2 mm: 0.78 and 1.00 mm.
c: 2 mm and more at outer corners, but at another spot than
inner ones: two screw patterns on one wall.
Every gap measured on this drawing; today's rule is 2 mm (C83).
